Analogous existing tests: `tests/unit/test_pass1_recall.py`, `tests/unit/workflow/test_pass1_usage.py` follow the `tests/unit/` convention
findings.finding: The plan names `tests/llm/test_pass1_warmup.py` as the test artifact, but no `tests/llm/` directory exists in the repository. Creating a file under a non-existent, non-standard directory will misplace the test and break CI discovery.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Address the checkpoint-restored warm-call scenario: either skip warm-up when the first candidate call would be checkpoint-served (check before serializing), or pick the first non-checkpoint call as the warm call, and add an AC/unit test covering this edge case.
evidence: pass1.py:471-475: 'cached = sizing.load_checkpoint(...) / if cached is not None: / resumed += 1 / return cached, []' — zero LLM calls, no cache write
Plan AC1: 'exactly one call completes before any pool submission and the rest fan out' — exercised via recording FakeRunner, which never hits checkpoints
Container path (pass1.py:226-227): uses _timed_pairing which calls passes.pass1_container directly, bypassing the checkpoint layer — not subject to this issue
findings.finding: The warm-then-fan-out mechanism has a hidden correctness gap when the selected 'warm' call is served from a checkpoint (load_checkpoint returns a cached result with zero LLM calls). In that case the cache prefix is never written, but the mechanism treats the call as successfully warm and submits only N-1 items to the pool — all of which then miss the cache on a cold run. The plan's AC only exercises this via a FakeRunner that always makes LLM calls, so this scenario is not covered.
findings.location: Approach section and AC1 — 'the first call completes before the pool starts'; also pass1.py:471-475 (_chunk checkpoint path)
scenarios: A large plan is reviewed twice in close succession; on the second run, the first chunk is checkpoint-restored. The warm call makes no LLM call, the cache is cold, and all N-1 fanned-out calls each pay a full cache-write miss — exactly the original problem, now with added serial latency.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Specify the exact token-estimation formula for the main-pool warm gate (e.g., `det_floor.est_tokens(ctx.plan_text)` as the shared-prefix proxy, matching the plan-bearing system prompt), so the gate threshold is unambiguous to implementers.
evidence: Plan text: 'when the estimated shared-prefix tokens >= CACHE_MIN_PREFIX_TOKENS and (chunks + agent criteria) >= 2'
Container gate (pass1.py:190): parent_tokens = det_floor.est_tokens(ctx.plan_text) + det_floor.est_tokens(roster) — explicit formula
Main pool: no analogous formula stated in the plan
findings.finding: The plan's gate condition references 'estimated shared-prefix tokens' without defining the formula used to compute it for the main pool, leaving implementers to guess. The container path has an explicit formula (est_tokens(ctx.plan_text) + est_tokens(roster)); the main pool needs an analogous, stated formula (presumably just est_tokens(ctx.plan_text), since the per-chunk rubric text is not shared) — but the plan is silent.
findings.location: Approach section — 'when the estimated shared-prefix tokens >= CACHE_MIN_PREFIX_TOKENS'
scenarios: An implementer uses the total prompt size (plan + chunk rubric) as the estimate, over-counting and always warming even for small plans where the plan text alone is below 4096 tokens.
An implementer uses only est_tokens(ctx.plan_text), which is correct, but the plan doesn't say so — another implementer uses a different proxy.
findings.suggested_fix: In the Approach section, replace 'estimated shared-prefix tokens' with 'est_tokens(ctx.plan_text) >= CACHE_MIN_PREFIX_TOKENS', mirroring the container gate's use of plan_tokens as the dominant shared-prefix component.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Specify which token-count components compose the 'estimated shared-prefix tokens' for the main pool gate (e.g., `det_floor.est_tokens(ctx.plan_text)` alone, or plan + system-prompt framing), matching the precision of the container analog at pass1.py:190.
evidence: Plan text: 'when the estimated shared-prefix tokens >= CACHE_MIN_PREFIX_TOKENS and (chunks + agent criteria) >= 2'
Container gate (pass1.py:190): parent_tokens = det_floor.est_tokens(ctx.plan_text) + det_floor.est_tokens(roster) — explicitly sums plan + roster
Main pool prefix is structurally different (no roster, different system framing); plan gives no analogous formula
ABSENCE: no formula, variable name, or component list is named for the main-pool prefix estimate
findings.finding: The plan references 'estimated shared-prefix tokens' as the gate input for the main pool warm, but never specifies which components are summed to produce that estimate. The container analog uses `det_floor.est_tokens(ctx.plan_text) + det_floor.est_tokens(roster)`, but the main pool's shared prefix includes the system prompt framing and potentially rubric chunk text — none of these components are named in the plan.
findings.location: Approach section: 'when the estimated shared-prefix tokens >= CACHE_MIN_PREFIX_TOKENS'
scenarios: Implementor uses only est_tokens(plan_text), under-counting and never warming on borderline plans
Implementor includes rubric chunk tokens, over-counting and warming on small plans that don't actually cache
Inconsistency between container and main-pool gate semantics goes undetected in tests (FakeRunner token estimates are synthetic)
findings.suggested_fix: Add to the Approach section: 'The shared-prefix estimate is `det_floor.est_tokens(ctx.plan_text)` (the plan is the dominant cacheable prefix for all main-pool calls; rubric framing is excluded to match the container gate's conservatism).'

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Clarify the warm-call selection rule in the Approach: specify whether it is always the first chunk (and what happens when chunks is empty), mirroring the precision of `pairings[0]` in the container path.
evidence: Approach: 'run the first single-turn chunk to completion serially (writing the cache prefix), then submit the remainder to the pool'
AC #1: 'the first call completes before the pool starts (checked: unit test asserting call-ordering via a recording runner)' — 'first call' is ambiguous about chunk vs agent
Container analog (pass1.py:226): 'bin_children = pairings[0]' — selection is unambiguous
ABSENCE: no statement of what to do when chunks is empty (only agent criteria remain) — whether to warm on an agent call or skip warming
findings.finding: The plan does not specify which call is selected as the warm call for the main pool. The container warm uses `pairings[0]` (first bin). For the main pool the candidates are a mix of single-turn chunks and agent futures; the plan says 'the first single-turn chunk' in the Approach but the AC says 'exactly one call completes before any pool submission' without naming the selection rule, and the testing section does not specify whether the warm call must be a chunk (not an agent criterion).
findings.location: Approach section: 'run the first single-turn chunk to completion serially'; AC #1
scenarios: Implementor warms on the first agent criterion instead of first chunk, serializing the most expensive call and defeating parallelism
Implementor skips warming when chunks is empty but agent count >= 2, silently losing the cache benefit for agent-only reviews
Test uses only chunk-based calls, never covering the chunks==0 edge case
findings.suggested_fix: Add: 'When chunks is non-empty, the warm call is chunks[0] (single-turn); when chunks is empty and only agent criteria remain, no warm is performed (gate yields False for agent-only reviews, as serializing an 85×-cost agent call forfeits more than it saves).'

evidence: 2 criterion line(s) bundle multiple deliverables with 'and' (split so each is independently verifiable).

The plan has no integration or smoke-test AC against a live model; E6(f) anti-FP exemptions (opt-in flag, no live boundary) do not apply because the gate fires by default on qualifying plans and the live LLM API is the boundary.
findings.finding: The plan cuts over the main pool's default execution path (from direct fan-out to warm-then-fan-out) when the gate conditions are met, and all four ACs are verified exclusively with a FakeRunner/stubbed-usage run. No AC exercises the new warm path end-to-end against a live LLM dependency, so the cache-write/read behavior (the core claim) is never proven in production conditions.
findings.location: Testing section and all four Acceptance Criteria
scenarios: FakeRunner passes call-ordering checks but the live API does not actually reuse the cached prefix (e.g. due to a header mismatch, a model version that doesn't support prompt caching, or a token-count estimation off-by-one). The plan ships green tests but zero measured cache improvement.
findings.suggested_fix: Add an AC such as: 'In a live integration smoke test (<=2 calls, real model endpoint), the second call's usage metadata shows cache_read_input_tokens > 0, confirming the warm prefix was reused.' Gate it on the same CACHE_MIN_PREFIX_TOKENS condition and mark it as an optional CI stage if cost is a concern, with a rationale comment.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Add or confirm a timeout on the warm call (matching the pool's per-call timeout) so a slow — not just failed — warm call also triggers the fan-out fallback; document the timeout value alongside CACHE_MIN_PREFIX_TOKENS.
evidence: 'run the first single-turn chunk to completion serially (writing the cache prefix), then submit the remainder to the pool'
'a non-systemic warm failure degrades to direct fan-out exactly as the container path does (pass1.py:203-212)'
AC3 covers exception failure only: 'A failing warm call degrades to today's direct fan-out' — no coverage of slow/hung warm call
findings.finding: The warm call is synchronous and blocking before pool submission, but no timeout is stated for it. A slow (non-failing) warm call delays all pool parallelism indefinitely — exception-based fallback does not protect against a hung or very-slow call.
scenarios: LLM endpoint is rate-limited or slow: warm call takes 60–120 s, all subsequent fan-out is delayed by that full duration with no escape hatch.
Network glitch causes a very-slow (not immediately erroring) response, stalling the entire review pipeline.
findings.suggested_fix: Wrap the warm call in a try/except that catches both exceptions and a concurrent.futures.TimeoutError (or equivalent asyncio.wait_for timeout), falling back to direct fan-out on either. Document the timeout as a configurable constant (e.g., WARM_CALL_TIMEOUT_S) alongside CACHE_MIN_PREFIX_TOKENS.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Add an observability hook (at minimum a structured log warning) when the warm call fails and fallback to direct fan-out is triggered, so operators can detect and diagnose degraded warm-up.
evidence: 'a non-systemic warm failure degrades to direct fan-out exactly as the container path does' — no mention of emitting a log warning, metric counter, or trace event on fallback
AC #4 mentions cache-write/read metrics for the happy path but nothing for the failure path
findings.finding: The plan specifies no observability (log, metric, or trace) when the warm call fails and execution falls back to direct fan-out. An operator has no way to detect that warm-up is silently degrading, potentially for every review run.
findings.location: Approach section / AC #3 ('A failing warm call degrades to today's direct fan-out')
scenarios: Warm call begins failing for all plans (e.g., provider error, token estimation bug) — operators see no signal; the feature silently loses all cache-warming benefit indefinitely.
A transient but frequent warm-call failure rate degrades performance undetected.
findings.suggested_fix: In the except branch that catches the warm-call failure (mirroring pass1.py:203-212), emit `logger.warning('pass1_warmup_failed', exc_info=True, extra={'plan_tokens': estimated_tokens})` and, if a metrics seam exists, increment a counter like `pass1_warmup_fallback_total`.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Specify a timeout (or reuse an existing per-call timeout) for the serial warm call so that a slow/hung warm does not block the fan-out beyond a bounded wait, falling back to direct fan-out if exceeded.
evidence: 'run the first single-turn chunk to completion serially' — no timeout or deadline mentioned
The plan notes the alternative of 'serializing the whole pool' was rejected to preserve parallelism, yet a hung warm call achieves the same worst-case outcome without bound
findings.finding: The serial warm call has no explicit timeout. If the LLM call hangs or is very slow, all subsequent fan-out calls are blocked from starting for the duration of that hang, potentially stalling the entire review.
findings.location: Approach section ('run the first single-turn chunk to completion serially')
scenarios: LLM provider is slow/degraded: warm call takes 60+ seconds; all pool calls are blocked waiting, making total review latency far worse than the direct fan-out baseline.
Network partition causes warm call to hang indefinitely with no timeout.
findings.suggested_fix: Wrap the serial warm call in the same per-call timeout already used by pool calls (or a configurable WARM_CALL_TIMEOUT_S). If the timeout expires, log the fallback and proceed directly to fan-out.

findings.finding: The plan's Problem section cites 'pass1.py:438,462-464' as where Pass-1 submits every chunk and AGENT future into the pool, but a Read probe shows lines 438 and 462-464 are budget-cap indeterminate construction and material_fingerprint/counter initialization — not pool submission code. The actual pool submission is at pass1.py:512-514. Any developer acting on these line numbers to place the warm gate would instrument the wrong location.
scenarios: A developer navigates to the cited lines to insert the warm gate and finds budget-cap infrastructure instead of the pool — misplaces the new warm-gate code.
A reviewer trying to verify the plan's problem statement reads lines 438/462-464 and cannot find the concurrent fan-out, undermining confidence in the plan's accuracy.
findings.suggested_fix: Replace `(src/rebar/llm/plan_review/pass1.py:438,462-464)` with `(src/rebar/llm/plan_review/pass1.py:488,512-514)` — line 488 computes `max_workers`, lines 512-514 open the ThreadPoolExecutor and submit `st_futs`/`ag_futs`.
